A saved preset describes intended configuration. Applied and runtime state are reported separately.

Advanced routing, access and request policies

Optional controls for backend pools, health checks, maintenance, forward authentication and path/body policies.

Path exposure

Leave this on profile default to keep a policy you did not edit. The ha-mcp profile then installs its preset (allowlist, Authorization on /api/mcp, a long SSE timeout). See the Home Assistant MCP guide. Restricted paths and profile block lists still apply.

Publication rules

Rules run from top to bottom. All specified conditions must match. Count records a match and continues. Block returns 403. Pass ends this list and continues with the remaining security checks.

Restricted paths

Optionally limit a URL prefix to specific IPs/CIDRs. Restricting Home Assistant /api also restricts /api/websocket and can block the web UI, Companion and external API clients. New applications have no automatic LAN restriction. One CIDR per line.

Request bodies

Leave empty to use the profile. A limit also refuses bodies of unknown length (chunked uploads), and blocking multipart breaks file uploads outside the allowed paths. This reduces exposure to request-parsing flaws; it does not replace patching.

Open this tab to load presets…

WAF rules

Edge network

Takes effect on the next Apply HAProxy (Edge changes).

Response headers

Real client IP behind a proxy

Only requests whose source is in Trusted proxies may replace their address with the header below; others keep their own. Without this, behind Cloudflare or a tunnel every client looks like the proxy to IP lists, GeoIP, CrowdSec and rate limits.

MQTT, RTSP, ...: one per line, name listen_port backend_host:backend_port [allow=CIDR,CIDR] [off]. Raw TCP: no HTTP rules apply; the IP blacklist does. Allow each listen port in Network → Firewall.

One per line, server_name backend_host:backend_port [allow=CIDR,CIDR] [proxy] [off]. Connections for that name (or *.domain) go to the backend still encrypted, with its own certificate; no HTTP rules apply. proxy sends PROXY protocol v2 (the backend must expect it). The name must not be an application's public host.

IP Blacklist

Local CIDRs and optional external lists → ip_blacklist.map. Sync refreshes the map; use Edge changes for a new HAProxy config.

Trusted internal CIDRs for feed fetch

Allow IPBL feeds hosted on internal DNS names resolving to these private ranges (split-DNS). Loopback and metadata addresses are always blocked.

IP Allowlist

Trusted CIDRs bypass IP blacklist and per-app HTTP rate limits when enabled.

Bot protection

Blocked UA map is written on Apply HAProxy (Edge changes).

GeoIP

When enabled, Sync / Apply resolve blacklist CIDRs to countries. ipinfo: optional GEOIP_IPINFO_TOKEN on the API host. maxmind: local GeoLite2-Country MMDB — see repository file docs/GEOIP.md.

GeoLite2 .mmdb or the MaxMind .tar.gz. Installed only after it opens and answers a test lookup.

Backup and restore

          
Backup and restore are not available in the web panel. Run the packaged commands from the appliance console or an SSH session with sudo.

          
sudo easy-waf-backup --dir /var/backups/easy-waf --keep 7

          
sudo easy-waf-restore /path/to/easy-waf-backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz

          
Restore replaces the database and appliance state. Use a protected, same-version archive and follow docs/BACKUP_RESTORE.md. The daily easy-waf-backup.timer keeps seven archives by default.

⚙ Edge changes

        
Apply renders from the database, validates with haproxy -c, writes the live config, and records a revision.

        

          
        

        

          
Config revisions

          
Successful Apply and Rollback; live file hash = current.

          
Rollback restores a previous edge configuration. Saved applications and settings stay unchanged; a later Apply or restart can replace this configuration.

Service-specific options live under Certificates (ACME, management TLS), CrowdSec (LAPI / SPOE), and Security (WAF, IP lists, GeoIP). Use Load from server here to fill all tabs from GET /api/v1/settings.

        

          
        

        

          
Monitoring

          
When enabled, Prometheus can scrape GET /metrics on this management service. Access is restricted by management_allowed_cidrs only (no JWT). See docs/MONITORING.md.

          
          
For passive polling of a Zabbix agent installed on this host, the managed rule allows TCP 10050 from RFC1918 and loopback. Keep the port off the WAN.

          
          

          

            
            
          

          
Zabbix firewall changes use the same 90s safety window as Network → Firewall: click Keep changes after apply, or the previous ruleset returns.

        

        

          
Notifications

          
Sent to a webhook (JSON), a Telegram chat, or both: a failed HAProxy apply, a backend server going down or coming back, a spike of blocked requests, and once a day certificates that failed to issue or renew or have fewer than 21 days left. Leave both empty to keep warnings in the journal only. The URL and token are not written to the log; redirects are not followed.
